children: KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia--AirAsia Group said it plans to raise up to $1 billion in the international debt market to restructure its debt and consolidate its balance-sheet.

The company also plans to raise 700 million ringgit, equivalent to $173.1 million, through local credit facilities, it said Wednesday, in response to media reports that its capital-raising activities were intended to fund operational shortfalls.

The funds will be used to consolidate existing facilities into a lower-cost debt structure with extended maturities, reducing interest expenses and securing liquidity for working capital, AirAsia said.
AirAsia raised about $300 million in March to extend debt maturities and reduce principal obligations.

The company said its 20% to 25% third quarter capacity adjustment is a response to seasonal weakness in regional travel, with capacity expected to ramp up toward peak and pre-war levels in the fourth quarter, the strongest travel window of the year.
AirAsia has returned 25 older, less fuel-efficient aircraft on favorable terms to reduce lease obligations and non-fuel costs.
In second quarter, the company recovered 70% of fuel-price increases through fare adjustments and lower non-fuel operating expenses.
